# Dart pattern matching, the idiomatic way

Curated by Skill Harbor — an official Dart-lang guide that teaches an agent to apply Dart 3 pattern matching idiomatically. Covers a pattern-selection strategy (which pattern type for JSON validation, URI/path segments, polymorphic payloads, records, algebraic data types, numeric ranges), switch statements vs. expressions, and the full pattern syntax (logical-or/and, relational, cast, null-check, wildcard, list/map/record/object patterns). Its real value is the pragmatic boundaries: six named anti-patterns (prefer `is` promotion over `if-case`, avoid gratuitous destructuring, don't silently drop malformed data…), plus verification workflows — exhaustiveness checking via `dart analyze` and runtime Map/JSON key-semantics checks. Honest caveats: the guidance is verified against the Dart 3 analyzer of its era and may drift as the language evolves; `dart analyze` cannot statically verify dynamic Map keys, so runtime checks remain necessary. Credit to its creator. Skill Harbor never reviews the code, review it yourself before use. Discovered via skills.sh.
